API reference

The module exports a factory, a custom element, a few registration hooks and some constants. Types ship in src/index.d.ts.

createBot()#

import { createBot } from '@kucukkanat/bots';

const bot = createBot(target, options);

target is an element (a canvas is made inside it), a selector string, or a <canvas> to draw into directly. options are the options. It returns a BotAvatar controller; new BotAvatar(target, options) does the same.

Methods#

MethodWhat it does
set(options)Change any options; the look eases into them. Pass undefined to drop one back to its default. Returns the bot.
setState(state)Switch state: default, listening, thinking, speaking, working, success, error, sleeping, or a registered one.
observe(event, data?)Tell it what the agent is doing and let it work out the rest: 'typing' ({ target }), 'sent', 'token' ({ text }: said with lip-sync, its tone read), 'tool' / 'tool-end' ({ name }), 'done', 'error' ({ message }), 'idle', 'reset'. Loads the affect module on first use. See Agent recipes.
say(text, { wpm, append })Lip-sync from text: the mouth shapes follow the words at wpm (words per minute). append: true adds to what it's already saying, for streamed text. Returns a Promise that resolves when it has finished talking.
react(expression, duration?)A moment's expression over any state: happy, joy, surprised, worried, sad, angry, smug, sleepy, confused, dizzy, love, or an object of face channels. Default 1.6 s.
speak(source?)The mouth follows audio: a MediaStream (mic), an <audio>/<video> element, or a Web Audio node from any AudioContext. Switches to speaking; speak() with nothing stops and restores the previous state.
setVoice(level)Drive the speaking mouth by hand, 0–1 (e.g. from TTS visemes); null for made-up chatter.
lookAt(target)Keep an eye on an element or a client-space point { x, y }; null to stop. The pointer still wins when it comes close.
poke()Hop and turn round, as a click does.
on(event, fn)Listen for an event (below). Returns a function that stops listening.
feature(name)Load an optional feature now rather than on first use. Resolves to its controller.
export(options?)Render an animation or still to a Blob. See Export.
toDataURL({ full?, scale? })PNG of the current frame.
draw()Draw one frame now (paused avatars, tests).
destroy()Stop, remove the canvas it made, and free its worker slot.

Properties#

PropertyValue
readyPromise that resolves to the bot once it has a renderer (a worker thread or the main thread).
dnaThe whole design as a short URL-safe code, bot1.….
optionsThe current, normalised options.
canvasThe canvas it draws into.
webglWhether its frames are painted with WebGL.
poseThe live pose (yaw, pitch, mouthOpen…), read-only.

Events#

const off = bot.on('land', () => playThud());
off(); // stop listening

el.addEventListener('bot-blink', (e) => console.log(e.detail));   // the same, as bubbling DOM events
EventWhen
pokeClicked or poke()d.
blinkBlinked.
jumpLeft the floor.
landLanded.
stateThe state changed; e.state is the new one.
say-start, say-endsay() started or finished talking.

Every event is also dispatched from the canvas as a bubbling DOM event named bot-<event>, so you can listen on any ancestor.

The <bot-avatar> element#

Importing the module defines <bot-avatar>. Every option is an attribute in kebab-case; booleans are present or absent (or "false"); grouped options take JSON.

<bot-avatar id="agent" type="cat" state="thinking" size="96" bow-tie fur='{"pattern":"spots"}'></bot-avatar>
<script type="module">
  const el = document.querySelector('#agent');
  el.setAttribute('state', 'speaking');   // attributes are live
  el.bot.say('Hello!');                   // the controller, for everything else
</script>
MemberWhat it is
botThe BotAvatar controller (after the element is connected).
poke(), react(), speak(), setVoice(), lookAt()Shortcuts to the controller.
dnaThe design's DNA code.
refresh()Re-read attributes and CSS variables (after changing --bot-* variables).

Registering your own#

FunctionAdds
registerShape(name, { path or points, color, label, faceY, faceScale })A shape, from SVG path data in a 100×100 box.
registerHat(name, { layers, width, lift })A hat, from layers of SVG path data with fill or stroke.
registerState(name, { pose, keyframes, duration, loop, blink })A state: a held pose or a keyframed loop.

See Plugins & packs for examples.

Other exports#

ExportWhat it is
BotAvatar, BotAvatarElement, defineBotAvatar(name?)The controller class, the element class, and a way to define the element under another tag name.
encodeDNA(options), decodeDNA(code)Options ⇄ DNA codes.
lookFromId(id)The look identity would give an id.
wearables()Everything that can be worn: { name, spot, label }, built-ins then hats from packs and plugins.
parseWear(list), wornList(options)A wear list ⇄ options. spotOf(name) says where a thing goes.
normalizeOptions(options)Flat options from grouped ones, presets, DNA and identity.
exportBot(bot, options)The function behind bot.export().
renderSettingsGlobal switches, set before the first avatar: workers (default true), maxWorkers (default 4), softwareWebGL.
renderStats{ drawn }: frames drawn so far on every thread, for benchmarks.
types, presets, paletteShape names, their labels and colours. BASE_TYPES is the first eighteen; creatures the cast's modules.
registerCreature(def)Add a creature in the cast's own format: outline, parts, temperament, defaults, morph, stages. See The cast.
geometryThe outline helpers the cast is built with: circle, poly, polarUnion, polar, param, superellipse, roundPoly, chaikin.
STATES, SHADINGS, HATS, GLASSES, EYE_STYLES, MOUTH_STYLES, BROWS, EAR_STYLES, FUR_PATTERNS, STYLES, EXPRESSIONSThe accepted values, for building UIs.
DEFAULTSThe default options.
BotSim, drawBot, resolveLook, restPoseThe simulation and the 2D renderer, for drawing frames yourself.

Framework entry points#

ImportGives you
@kucukkanat/botsEverything above; defines <bot-avatar>.
@kucukkanat/bots/react<BotAvatar> component.
@kucukkanat/bots/vueBotAvatar component.
@kucukkanat/bots/sveltebot action.
@kucukkanat/bots/exportexportStickers() and the exporters.

Usage for each is in Frameworks.
